<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD defines a standard source URL pointing to an archived release tarball from the official GitLab instance of the Monado project (`gitlab.freedesktop.org`). The source is a static archive using a tagged version (`v${pkgver}`), and the SHA-256 checksum is provided and matches the expected value for integrity verification.

During `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` and `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, only the top-level variables and `pkgver()` (if present) are evaluated. This PKGBUILD has no executable code in the global scope or within a `pkgver()` function — it only sets static variables. There is no command substitution, no network activity beyond the declared source download (which is expected), and no data exfiltration mechanisms active during sourcing.

The presence of `sha256sums` with a valid hash further ensures that the downloaded source integrity can be verified later in the build process, although even if it were set to 'SKIP', that alone would not make this stage unsafe per the gate criteria.
</details>

<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The provided PKGBUILD file is consistent with standard Arch User Repository (AUR) packaging practices. It defines a package for Monado, an open-source OpenXR runtime, with two subpackages: `monado` and `monado-doc`. The source is fetched from the official GitLab repository under freedesktop.org, a trusted entity in the open-source graphics and display server ecosystem. The source URL points to a specific tagged release (`v25.1.0`), ensuring reproducibility, and the SHA256 checksum is provided and matches the expected value.

The build process uses CMake as expected, with standard flags to enable documentation building and set the installation prefix. The `package_monado` and `package_monado-doc` functions perform straightforward installations into the package directory, with no suspicious file operations, network access, or execution of external scripts. Documentation is installed into `/usr/share/doc/monado` using standard `cp` and `install` commands. There are no uses of `eval`, `curl`, `wget`, `base64`, or other potentially dangerous constructs. All dependencies listed are relevant to the functionality of an XR runtime, including graphics, input, and system integration libraries.

The checksum is valid and the source is from the project's official upstream. While the `source` array uses a tarball from a versioned release (not a VCS checkout), this is normal and secure when paired with a correct checksum. No code is generated or downloaded at build time beyond what is included in the source archive. The package also follows proper packaging guidelines by splitting documentation into a separate package and using appropriate permissions.
</details>
